subtitle: Rammohun Roy and the First Fire of the Bengal Renaissance

panels.shot: epic three-quarter view, low-angle wide, young Rammohun framed by palm trees and old temple spires, half in shadow, half in dawn light
panels.action: Young Rammohun Roy stands alone on a rural Bengal path, palm leaves swaying above and distant temple towers rising behind him, his eyes steady, a scroll in one hand and a worn Persian manuscript in the other.

dialogue.text: In an age of kings and company clerks, when few dared to ask, one man—Rammohun Roy—turned to Persian, Sanskrit, Bengali and English to ask a dangerous question: Why?

i18n.hi: राजाओं और कंपनी क्लर्कों के समय में, जब कोई पूछने की जुर्रत न करे, एक आदमी—राममोहन राय—ने फ़ारसी, संस्कृत, बांग्ला और अंग्रेज़ी में एक खतरनाक सवाल किया: क्यों?

panels.shot: intimate interior wide, candlelit, child’s-eye level
panels.action: In a modest house at Radhanagar, young Rammohun sits by an oil lamp, tracing letters in Bengali and Sanskrit on palm-leaf manuscripts as an elder’s shadowy hand points to script on a wooden board.

dialogue.text: Rammohun Roy was born in 1772 in Radhanagar, into a world of village fields, temple bells and Mughal decrees, learning Bengali and Sanskrit by lamplight as the old order slowly frayed.

i18n.hi: राममोहन राय 1772 में राधानगर में जन्मे—गाँव के खेत, मंदिर की घंटियाँ, मुग़ल फ़रमानों की दुनिया में—दीये की रोशनी में बांग्ला- संस्कृत सीखे, जबकि पुराना निज़ाम धीरे-धीरे टूट रहा था।

panels.shot: medium shot, side view, inside a Persian madrasa-style classroom
panels.action: A slightly older Rammohun sits cross-legged in a Persian and Arabic class, listening intently as a bearded teacher gestures to flowing script on a hanging cloth, while other boys whisper around him.

dialogue.text: Soon he was sent to study Persian and Arabic, stepping into the language of Mughal courts and Islamic theology, absorbing verses and arguments that would become weapons in a later battle of ideas.

i18n.hi: जल्दी ही उसे फ़ारसी और अरबी पढ़ने भेजा गया—मुग़ल दरबार और इस्लामी इल्म की ज़बान में—जहाँ उसने ऐसे शेर और दलीलें सीखी जो आगे चलकर ख़यालों की जंग में हथियार बनेंगी।

panels.shot: tight three-quarter, contemplative, in a Varanasi ghat setting
panels.action: Young adult Rammohun stands on the steps of a ghat in Varanasi, watching priests perform rituals under the smoke of incense and the glow of evening lamps, his face calm but questioning.

dialogue.text: In Varanasi he studied Sanskrit and saw the daily rhythm of ritual and caste. He learned the shastras deeply, but their practice stirred in him not blind devotion, but a quiet unease.

i18n.hi: वाराणसी में उसने संस्कृत पढ़ी और रोज़मर्रा की पूजा- पाठ, जाति-व्यवस्था का ताल देखा। उसने शास्त्र गहराई से समझे, पर उनकी रीति ने अँधा भरोसा नहीं, भीतर एक हल्की बेचैनी जगाई।

panels.shot: slow push-in, interior desk shot, quill poised over paper
panels.action: In a dim room in Patna around 1803, Rammohun sits at a wooden desk with Persian papers spread before him, a quill hovering as if hesitating before the first line of a new treatise.

dialogue.text: Around 1803, in Patna, his studies turned into revolt on paper. In Persian he began Tuhfat ul Muwahhidin, a bold gift to monotheists, arguing that superstition had smothered true religion.

i18n.hi: 1803 के आस-पास पटना में उसकी पढ़ाई काग़ज़ पर बग़ावत बन गई। उसने फ़ारसी में ‘तूहफ़तुल मुवह्हिदीन’ शुरू की—एक दिलेर तोहफ़ा एकेश्वरवादियों को—दावा करते हुए कि अंधविश्वास ने सच्चे धर्म को दबा दिया है।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder close-up on manuscript lines, candle flicker
panels.action: From behind his shoulder, we see lines of Persian script flowing across the page, candlelight reflecting on the ink as his hand moves steadily, the room sparse and focused.

dialogue.text: In Tuhfat ul Muwahhidin he used reason and scripture to question idol worship and miracles, arguing across traditions that God was one and that blind custom betrayed both faith and mind.

i18n.hi: ‘तूहफ़तुल मुवह्हिदीन’ में उसने तर्क और धर्मग्रंथ से मूर्ति-पूजा और करामात पर सवाल उठाए, अलग-अलग मज़हबों से बहस करते हुए कहा कि ख़ुदा एक है और अंधी रस्में ईमान और समझ दोनों से गद्दारी हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot in East India Company office, crowded clerks and ledgers
panels.action: In a Calcutta Company office, Rammohun, now a composed young man, sits among British and Indian clerks, leafing through a Persian revenue report as a window shows ships’ masts on the river outside.

dialogue.text: By the 1810s he worked for the East India Company, translating and handling revenue. He moved easily between British offices and Bengali lanes, watching colonial power tighten its grip.

i18n.hi: 1810 के दशक तक वह ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी में काम कर रहा था—तरजमे और लगान का काम संभालते हुए। वह ब्रिटिश दफ़्तरों और बांग्ला मुहल्लों के बीच आसानी से चलता, और देखता कि हुकूमत कैसे अपनी पकड़ कस रही है।

panels.shot: interior wide, informal gathering, lamplit Calcutta drawing room
panels.action: In a Calcutta room around 1815, Rammohun sits among a small circle of Indian friends, books in several languages piled at the center, his hand raised, others listening in thoughtful silence.

dialogue.text: Around 1815 he began the Atmiya Sabha—an intimate society of friends in Calcutta—where men met to debate Upanishadic monotheism, ethics and reform, beyond the noise of orthodox assemblies.

i18n.hi: 1815 के आसपास उसने कलकत्ता में आत्मीय सभा शुरू की—दोस्तों की छोटी सी महफ़िल—जहाँ लोग उपनिषदों के एकेश्वरवाद, नैतिकता और सुधार पर बहस करते, सनातनी जमावड़ों की शोर से दूर।

panels.shot: slow push-in on his face, mixture of conviction and restraint
panels.action: Rammohun leans forward in the gathering, brows knit in concentration, as if weighing new ideas against inherited duties, while a faint sound of street vendors drifts in from outside.

dialogue.speaker: rammohun_roy
dialogue.text: If our shastras speak of one supreme, why do we bow before so many stones?

i18n.hi: जब शास्त्र एक सर्वोच्च की बात करें, फिर हम इतने पत्थरों को क्यों माथा टेकें?

panels.shot: dynamic interior wide, printing press in motion
panels.action: Inside a early nineteenth-century Calcutta printing room, Rammohun stands beside a wooden press as workers ink type, stacks of freshly printed Bengali sheets resting on a table.

dialogue.text: He understood that private debate was not enough. Through journals like Sambad Kaumudi in Bengali and Mirat-ul-Akhbar in Persian, he carried argument into the streets and courtyards.

i18n.hi: उसे समझ आया कि बंद कमरे की बहस काफी नहीं। ‘संवाद कौमुदी’ जैसे बांग्ला अख़बार और फ़ारसी ‘मिरात-उल-अख़बार’ के ज़रिए उसने तर्क को गली-कूचों तक पहुँचा दिया।

panels.shot: street-level wide, papers being handed out in a Calcutta bazaar
panels.action: In a bustling Calcutta bazaar, vendors hand out folded newspapers; a passerby reads a bold column while, in the background, Rammohun walks quietly, observing reactions.

dialogue.text: In those pages he criticized abuses, defended monotheism and argued for cautious reform, using print as a new sabha—a public hall where peasants, pundits and clerks could all hear the question why.

i18n.hi: इन पन्नों में उसने ज़ुल्मों पर चोट की, एकेश्वरवाद की हिमायत की और संभलकर सुधार की बात की—छापाखाना को नई सभा बना दिया, जहाँ किसान, पंडित और क्लर्क सब ‘क्यों’ का सवाल सुन सकें।

panels.shot: intense desk close-up, English letter, quill mid-stroke
panels.action: In 1823, Rammohun sits at a desk with an English draft before him, pen poised over the salutation, the faint outline of Fort William visible through a high window.

dialogue.text: In 1823 he wrote to Lord Amherst, urging Western scientific education in Bengal. He wanted Sanskrit learning, but also mathematics, philosophy and modern science in the new government college.

i18n.hi: 1823 में उसने लॉर्ड अमहर्स्ट को लिखकर बंगाल में पाश्चात्य वैज्ञानिक शिक्षा की गुहार की। वह संस्कृत शिक्षा भी चाहता था, पर साथ में गणित, दर्शन और आधुनिक विज्ञान नए सरकारी कॉलेज में।

panels.shot: three-quarter shot, slight tension in posture, colonial architecture backdrop
panels.action: Outside a grand colonial building, Rammohun stands on the steps, papers in hand, looking up at the columns with a mix of pragmatism and caution as British officials pass by.

dialogue.text: He worked within colonial institutions, believing they could spread useful knowledge, yet he was no simple collaborator, pressing them to open their doors wider than they wished.

i18n.hi: वह औपनिवेशिक दफ़्तरों के भीतर ही काम करता रहा, मानते हुए कि उनसे काम की विद्या फैल सकती है; पर वह सीधा सहयोगी नहीं था—इन पर दबाव डालता रहा कि अपने दरवाज़े उनकी चाहत से ज़्यादा खोलें।

panels.shot: somber interior wide, meeting room with mixed group listening
panels.action: In a Calcutta hall in 1828, Rammohun stands before a group of Indian associates, a simple wooden platform beneath him, as he calmly outlines a plan for a new monotheistic association.

dialogue.text: In 1828 he helped found the Brahmo Sabha, a new space in Calcutta for worship of a single, formless God, drawing on Upanishadic ideas and his long critique of idolatry.

i18n.hi: 1828 में उसने कलकत्ता में ब्रह्मो सभा की बुनियाद में हाथ बँटाया—एक नई जगह, जहाँ निराकार, एकमात्र ईश्वर की पूजा हो—उपनिषदों से ताक़त लेकर और मूर्ति-पूजा पर उसकी पुरानी तनक़ीद के सहारे।

panels.shot: reverent interior wide, trust deed signing, table central
panels.action: On January 8, 1830, inside a formal Calcutta room, Rammohun sits with associates around a table, signing a thick document—the Brahmo Sabha Trust Deed—while others watch seriously.

dialogue.text: The Brahmo Sabha Trust Deed of 1830 bound the institution to monotheistic worship and ethical living. It turned his arguments into an enduring framework rather than a passing protest.

i18n.hi: 1830 के ब्रह्मो सभा ट्रस्ट डीड ने संस्था को एकेश्वर-पूजा और नैतिक जीवन से बाँध दिया। उसकी दलीलों को यह सिर्फ़ एक धरना नहीं, बल्कि टिकाऊ ढाँचा बना गया।

panels.shot: balanced interior medium shot, showing him in quiet prayer stance
panels.action: Inside the Sabha hall, Rammohun stands with others in simple, text-focused worship, no images on the walls, his hands joined loosely, eyes closed in reflective stillness.

dialogue.text: Yet his reform was not total. He questioned idols and certain customs, but remained cautious on caste and on women’s property, his own limits marking the edges of this first wave of change.

i18n.hi: फिर भी उसका सुधार पूरा नहीं था। उसने मूर्तियों और कुछ रस्मों को चुनौती दी, लेकिन जाति और औरतों की मिल्कियत पर संभलकर रहा—उसकी अपनी सीमाएँ इस पहली लहर की हदें तय करती रहीं।

panels.shot: poised desk shot, multiple language manuscripts scattered
panels.action: Rammohun sits later in life at a broad table, surrounded by manuscripts and newspapers in Persian, Bengali, Sanskrit and English, his gaze distant as if measuring what has been done against what remains.

dialogue.text: He had woven a dialogue across four languages, from Tuhfat ul Muwahhidin to his journals and Sabha, but the society around him changed slowly, resisting, reshaping and sometimes ignoring his pleas.

i18n.hi: उसने चार ज़बानों में एक संवाद बुना—‘तूहफ़तुल मुवह्हिदीन’ से लेकर अख़बारों और सभा तक—पर उसके आस-पास का समाज धीमे-धीमे बदला, कभी टकराया, कभी ढला और कई बार उसकी पुकार अनसुनी कर दी।

panels.shot: melancholic yet dignified exterior, Bristol street with Indian figure
panels.action: In a Bristol street late in his life, Rammohun walks in Indian dress beneath grey English skies, unfamiliar buildings towering as passersby glance at the foreign scholar.

dialogue.text: His journey carried him even to Bristol in England, where he died in 1833, far from Bengal, leaving behind not a completed revolution but a set of questions that would outlive him.

i18n.hi: उसका सफ़र उसे इंग्लैंड के ब्रिस्टल तक ले गया, जहाँ 1833 में उसकी मौत हुई—बंगाल से दूर—पीछे छोड़कर कोई पूरी हुई इंक़लाब नहीं, बल्कि ऐसे सवालों का गुच्छा जो उसके बाद भी ज़िंदा रहे।

panels.shot: epic pull-back, composite of Sabha hall, printed pages and quiet river
panels.action: The image blends the Brahmo Sabha hall, a printing press with scattered pages, and the calm course of a Bengal river at sunset, with Rammohun’s figure small but steady at the center.

dialogue.text: Rammohun Roy did not tear the old world down; he opened a space inside it where asking why was an act of devotion, a reminder that reform often begins with one mind daring to question aloud.

i18n.hi: राममोहन राय ने पुरानी दुनिया को ढहा नहीं दिया; उसने उसके भीतर एक जगह खोल दी जहाँ ‘क्यों’ पूछना ही भक्ति का काम बन गया—याद दिलाते हुए कि सुधार अक्सर वहीं से शुरू होता है, जहाँ एक दिमाग़ खुले आम सवाल उठाने की हिम्मत करे।

subtitle_i18n.en: Rammohun Roy and the First Fire of the Bengal Renaissance
subtitle_i18n.hi: राममोहन राय और बंगाल पुनर्जागरण की पहली चिंगारी
